prompt.brief: Design a fair, abuse-resistant flash-distribution system that gives away six million vouchers or burgers in one hour while keeping inventory, eligibility, and redemption correct under extreme concurrency.
successSignals: Define eligibility, fairness, admission, reservation, redemption, expiry, and inventory ledgers with an idempotency key per user/campaign.
Absorb millions of arrivals with waiting-room admission, bot defenses, quotas, randomized or timestamped ordering, and bounded queues.
Keep the hot path small and asynchronous; make inventory allocation atomic and reconcile abandoned reservations and store redemptions durably.
Explain regional capacity, retries, fraud, queue failure, campaign pause/resume, observability, and a transparent sold-out mode.

functional: Admit eligible users, issue a fair position/token, reserve an item, confirm redemption, and expose queue and reservation status.
Enforce one-per-user/device limits, campaign windows, inventory variants, expiration, cancellation, and store/fulfillment handoff.
Make retries safe, prevent oversell and double redemption, audit decisions, and recover from queue, payment-free fulfillment, or region failures.
nonFunctional: Absorb at least 10 million arrival attempts in an hour while keeping allocation correctness and a bounded admission response.
Distribute six million successful allocations without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 10M arrivals/hour and 6M available items across thousands of stores
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Fair, abuse-resistant flash-distribution system commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Fair, abuse-resistant flash-distribution system writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Fair, abuse-resistant flash-distribution system by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Fair, abuse-resistant flash-distribution system work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Fair, abuse-resistant flash-distribution system projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Fair, abuse-resistant flash-distribution system projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
